topic: Common-neighborhood energy of commuting graphs, surface graphs and disjoint unions of cliques
title: Proofs of Nath–Fasfous–Das–Shang's commuting and surface conjectures, and a sharp form of Tak–Dutta–Nath's clique theorem

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: For Nath–Fasfous–Das–Shang's Conjectures 1–3 (Symmetry 13 (2021), 1651, Section 4, p. 11), we prove the surface and commuting-graph statements and give an alternative proof with exact equality cases for Tak–Dutta–Nath's prior clique result (arXiv:2605.22160v1 (2026), Theorem 5.4, pp. 14–15). Every planar or toroidal graph is non-CN-hyperenergetic. For every finite nonabelian group, its noncentral commuting graph satisfies E_CN ≤ n(n-z-2) < 2(n-1)(n-2), where n counts noncentral elements and z counts central elements; the same bound holds for every finite noncommutative ring, without an identity assumption. The group argument combines the published estimate E_CN ≤ 4m with a proper-centralizer count. A neighborhood-clique decomposition proves the surface statement. For a union of cliques, equality with the complete-graph benchmark occurs exactly for one clique or two isolated vertices.
summary: Proofs of the surface and commuting-graph conjectures, a center-dependent bound for all finite noncommutative rings, centralizer-profile and least-prime-divisor refinements, and an alternative proof with all equality cases for the previously established clique-union conclusion.
